entries.symptom: Synthetic save migration preflight failed because the transform appeared to set save_version=2 but validation still read save_version=1.
entries.root_cause: JsonValue::set is append-only and JsonValue::require returns the first matching key, so adding a second save_version created duplicate schema keys and left the original version authoritative.
entries.fix: Added fail-closed JsonValue::replace for existing object fields and changed migration transforms to replace save_version rather than append a duplicate key.
entries.verification: Full canonical preflight passed on commit dda0248bde9f730710bb630e1b62acb755235ef3 after the repair; all 23 simulation tests passed including ordered migration fixtures.
entries.residual_risk: Future migration transforms can still misuse append-only set for other existing schema keys unless they follow the same replace-existing-field rule; schema migrations should review every modified existing key for replacement semantics.

entries.symptom: Issue #235 finding 2 (post-merge Codex review of PR #234): AEverwardPlayerController::AdvanceControlledHover() called CommandSetControlledHoverVelocityMetersPerSecond() directly from APlayerController::Tick(), once per render frame, even though the implementation/docs claimed a fixed-step velocity governor.
entries.root_cause: The authoritative fixed-step boundary lives in UProbeSimulationAdapter::TickComponent()'s own accumulator loop (Core->advance_wall_ticks()/Manipulators->advance()), which can run zero, one, or many iterations within a single render frame depending on frame rate. Applying the hover altitude correction once per render frame instead of once per elapsed fixed step made the resulting trajectory depend on frame rate rather than the deterministic tick sequence, violating the documented determinism invariant whenever multiple fixed steps landed in one low-framerate frame.
entries.fix: Moved the correction itself into UProbeSimulationAdapter::AdvanceControlledHoverGovernorFixedStep(), called once per elapsed fixed step from inside TickComponent()'s existing while loop, right after Core->advance_wall_ticks(). The player controller now only configures the governor (SetControlledHoverGovernorEngaged()) and polls a sequence-numbered GetControlledHoverGovernorNotice() once per frame purely to detect a fixed-step rejection and keep the toggle/HUD state in sync, following the same sequence-number change-detection pattern GetLastAutomationNotice() already established.
entries.verification: Full canonical preflight GREEN (control_plane, regression_memory, foundation, configure/build/test_simulation, tooling_tests, prototype_exit_gate, golden all PASS) on top of main commit e5392b7c345e2a39afd7d36c46e1f84783fd5385; all 29 src/simulation ctest suites passed; tools/test_controlled_hover_player_loop_surface.py updated and passing, including a new test asserting the correction call is issued from inside TickComponent()'s fixed-step loop after Core->advance_wall_ticks() rather than from the player controller.
entries.residual_risk: Controlled descent (AdvanceControlledDescent()) and Jose Take the Wheel (AdvanceJoseTakeTheWheel()) carried the same latent render-cadence dependency this fix removed from hover; issue #239 (see the controlled-descent-jose-render-cadence-dependent-correction entry below) closed that gap for both. No Unreal scene with a registered planetary body exists yet to exercise any of the three in PIE, so this remains implemented/Product-Reality-pending automated correctness rather than a PIE-verified fix.

entries.symptom: Issue #239 (follow-up named by the controlled-hover-render-cadence-dependent-correction entry's own residual_risk): AEverwardPlayerController::AdvanceControlledDescent() and AdvanceJoseTakeTheWheel() still called CommandSetControlledDescentVelocityMetersPerSecond()/GetJoseGuidanceCommand()+CommandSetVelocityMetersPerSecond() directly from APlayerController::Tick(), once per render frame, after #238 had already moved controlled hover's equivalent correction onto the adapter's fixed-step boundary.
entries.root_cause: Same as the hover defect: the authoritative fixed-step boundary lives in UProbeSimulationAdapter::TickComponent()'s own accumulator loop (Core->advance_wall_ticks()/Manipulators->advance()), which can run zero, one, or many iterations within a single render frame depending on frame rate. Re-evaluating the descent velocity cap or the José guidance/arrival decision once per render frame instead of once per elapsed fixed step made the resulting trajectory (and, for Jose, the exact tick an arrival/rejection is detected) depend on frame rate rather than the deterministic tick sequence.
entries.fix: Reused #238's governor pattern for both paths rather than inventing a second scheduler. Controlled descent: UProbeSimulationAdapter::AdvanceControlledDescentGovernorFixedStep() re-applies the velocity cap once per elapsed fixed step from inside TickComponent()'s existing while loop, right after AdvanceControlledHoverGovernorFixedStep(); the controller only configures the governor (SetControlledDescentGovernorEngaged()) and polls GetControlledDescentGovernorNotice(). Jose Take the Wheel needed a destination-autopilot-shaped governor rather than a plain velocity governor, since it also has to detect the player's target selection changing mid-flight and distinguish Arrived/DestinationUnresolved/DestinationNotFound/CommandRejected for its player-facing message: UProbeSimulationAdapter::AdvanceJoseAutopilotGovernorFixedStep() re-evaluates GetJoseGuidanceCommand() and issues/stops CommandSetVelocityMetersPerSecond() once per elapsed fixed step; the controller only configures the governor (SetJoseAutopilotGovernorEngaged()) and polls a new sequence-numbered GetJoseAutopilotGovernorNotice() (carrying an EEverwardJoseAutopilotStopReason so the exact prior player-facing messages are unchanged) purely to detect a fixed-step stop and keep the toggle/HUD state in sync -- the same sequence-number change-detection pattern GetControlledHoverGovernorNotice() already established. A Codex review on the PR caught a subtler instance of the same class of bug in the first version of this fix: the terminal outcomes (selection changed / arrived / destination unresolved or not found) disengaged the governor but left the probe's last commanded velocity active until the controller polled the notice on a later render tick, so the stop timing was still render-cadence dependent. AdvanceJoseAutopilotGovernorFixedStep() now issues CommandSetVelocityMetersPerSecond(FVector::ZeroVector) synchronously in the same fixed step it detects each terminal stop, and the controller's corresponding CancelJoseTakeTheWheel() calls no longer redundantly re-stop velocity (bStopVelocity=false in every governor-detected branch).
entries.verification: Full canonical preflight GREEN (control_plane, regression_memory, foundation, configure/build/test_simulation, tooling_tests, prototype_exit_gate, golden all PASS) on top of main commit 6cd0ebf9e5653a30217d5715d3d75ba144da69dd; all 29 src/simulation ctest suites passed (unaffected -- this is Unreal-adapter-only); tools/test_controlled_descent_player_loop_surface.py and tools/test_jose_autopilot_source_contract.py updated and passing, each gaining a new test asserting the correction/guidance call is issued from inside TickComponent()'s fixed-step loop after Core->advance_wall_ticks() rather than from the player controller, mirroring test_controlled_hover_player_loop_surface.py's existing regression test.
entries.residual_risk: No Unreal scene with a registered planetary body exists yet to exercise controlled descent or Jose in PIE, so this remains implemented/Product-Reality-pending automated correctness rather than a PIE-verified fix. Mining auto-approach (AdvanceAutoApproachMiningTarget()) was out of scope for issue #239 and has not been audited for the same render-cadence dependency.
